posts.content:
New from CARSI: Australian H5 bird flu awareness for restoration, cleaning, IAQ and facility teams is now live.

This is practical readiness training built on official Australian Government advice. The goal is not alarm. It is evidence, worker safety, documentation and clear professional boundaries.

The course teaches the behaviour that matters first: if you find sick or dead birds or animals, do not touch them, record what you see, and report them to the 24-hour Emergency Animal Disease Hotline on 1800 675 888.

It then works through worker safety and PPE, clean-before-disinfect discipline, clean and dirty zones, field documentation, and where a restoration professional's role begins and ends.

Enrol or read the full readiness overview:
https://carsi.com.au/courses/avian-influenza-awareness-restoration-iaq-facilities?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=carsi-h5-launch

5 things every restoration and facilities professional should know about H5 bird flu

1. Reporting comes before cleaning. If you find sick or dead birds or animals, do not touch them, record what you see, and report them to the Emergency Animal Disease Hotline on 1800 675 888.

2. Clean first, disinfect second, document third. Cleaning before disinfection is a core control principle.

3. You work under authority direction, not instead of it. Restoration and IAQ members can assist with risk assessment, documentation, containment planning, cleaning records, disinfection records and client communication under the direction of the responding authorities.

4. Worker safety is the job, not an add-on. The course covers WHS, PPE, fit checking, hygiene and exposure response.

5. Know your boundaries. Professionals support government, veterinary, wildlife and public-health authorities; they never replace them. Any disinfection method, including dry fogging, is label-led and SDS-led.

Everything above is exactly what the new CARSI course teaches:
https://carsi.com.au/courses/avian-influenza-awareness-restoration-iaq-facilities?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=carsi-h5-launch

A dead bird is not a cleanup job first. It is a reporting job first.

The reporting pathway is simple, and it is the same for everyone:

- Do not touch sick or dead birds or animals.
- Avoid contact.
- Record what you see.
- Report it to the Emergency Animal Disease Hotline: 1800 675 888.

Our reporting-pathway infographic lays this out in one image you can keep on site or share with your team. It is drawn straight from official Australian Government advice.

See the full pathway and the readiness course:
https://carsi.com.au/avian-influenza-readiness?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=carsi-h5-launch

Australia's H5 message should stay calm and official-source led.

As of the DAFF update of 5 July 2026, DAFF reported six confirmed H5 detections in wild birds - four in Western Australia, one in South Australia and one in New South Wales. DAFF states there is no evidence of mass mortality and no evidence of infection in poultry or the wider agriculture industry. The Australian Centre for Disease Control states the current risk to people in Australia is low.

Please check current DAFF advice for the latest status.

What professionals can do now is prepare: know the reporting pathway, know your PPE, and know your boundaries. That is what the CARSI readiness course is for.
https://carsi.com.au/avian-influenza-readiness?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=carsi-h5-launch

One sentence carries most of the discipline in this work: clean first, disinfect second, document third.

Cleaning before disinfection is a core control principle. Source removal and detergent cleaning come before any disinfectant, because a disinfectant works on a cleaned surface, not on organic load. The documentation then records what was actually done - product, dilution, contact time, operator and PPE.

The CARSI course walks through this sequence the way a job runs, not the way a brochure reads.
https://carsi.com.au/courses/avian-influenza-awareness-restoration-iaq-facilities?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=carsi-h5-launch

Who is this course for?

- Restoration technicians and supervisors.
- Commercial and specialised cleaning teams.
- Indoor air quality (IAQ) professionals.
- Facility, strata and property managers who oversee sites and contractors.

If your work could put you near a site where sick or dead birds are found, this course gives you the reporting pathway, the worker-safety controls and the documentation habits to respond properly - under authority direction.

It is self-paced and Australian-produced.
https://carsi.com.au/courses/avian-influenza-awareness-restoration-iaq-facilities?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=carsi-h5-launch

Before any surface is touched, the question is whether the worker is protected.

The CARSI H5 readiness course puts worker safety first: WHS risk assessment, PPE selection, fit checking, hygiene and exposure response. Required PPE follows the site's hazard assessment - it is not guesswork and it is stated before work begins.

Safe work is not the reward for a good job. It is the condition for starting one.
https://carsi.com.au/courses/avian-influenza-awareness-restoration-iaq-facilities?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=carsi-h5-launch

The most professional thing a restoration business can say on an H5 site is where its role ends.

Restoration and IAQ members can assist with risk assessment, documentation, containment planning, cleaning records, disinfection records and client communication - under authority direction. They do not replace government, veterinary, wildlife or public-health authorities, and they should never be marketed as if they do.

The course teaches those boundaries as clearly as it teaches the tasks.
https://carsi.com.au/courses/avian-influenza-awareness-restoration-iaq-facilities?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=carsi-h5-launch

If it is not documented, it did not happen - at least not for the client, the insurer or the authority.

CARSI's readiness pathway pairs with RestoreAssist field documentation: authority contacted and time, observations without handling, exclusion-zone photos, worker roster, PPE and fit-check notes, clean and dirty zone plans, cleaning and disinfection logs, and any product, batch, dilution and contact time. Exceptions and limitations are recorded too.

Good records are how professional site work becomes a defensible record.
https://carsi.com.au/avian-influenza-readiness?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=carsi-h5-launch

Watch the 7-minute narrated overview of CARSI's H5 bird flu readiness course - what it covers, who it is for, and why reporting always comes first.

Do not touch. Record. Report: 1800 675 888.
https://carsi.com.au/courses/avian-influenza-awareness-restoration-iaq-facilities?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=carsi-h5-launch
